rule: **C4 Unresolved references are preserved.** A call the tool cannot resolve is still emitted as a low guess (`recv.m`, `.m`, a bare name). It is never dropped and never promoted to a resolved ID. Silence in the graph means no call, or a `coverage` note. **C7 Complete edges.** Caller and callee are never empty. The line is the line of the callee's name, per the ID-format rules. **low**: a guess — receiver of unknown type (`recv.m`, `.m`), or a bare name not found in the scan.
notes: C4: `prepare_env`, `puts` and `bootstrap` are bare names not found in the scan -> bare-name low guesses (tier low: "a bare name not found in the scan"), never dropped. Legacy has no written external superclass/include/reopen, so the Ruby note's `Scope#m` medium rule does not apply (it lists only external superclass, include, reopened external class and computed superclass). SPEC gives Ruby no builtin/Kernel naming rule, so `puts` is an unresolved bare name. C7: file-level calls have the non-empty caller `lib/legacy`.
